_comment: Preguntas ORIGINALES tipo NIE del capítulo 1.5. No son preguntas reales del examen. Comprueba con tu edición 2027.

questions.scenario: Under s. 53 YJCEA 1999, what is the general rule on competence of witnesses?
options: Everyone is competent unless unable to understand questions and give answers that can be understood
Only people who can swear an oath are competent

questions.scenario: A 12-year-old witness understands questions and gives clear answers. How will she give evidence?
GRANT is charged with assaulting his wife. She refuses to give evidence for the prosecution. Which is correct?
options: She is compellable because the offence involves an assault on her
She can only give evidence for the defence
explanations: She is compellable in this offence.

questions.scenario: FORD is charged with burglary of his neighbour's house. His wife saw him leave with a bag. Is she compellable for the prosecution?
options: No – burglary of a neighbour is not a specified offence; she is competent but not compellable

questions.scenario: A wife is charged jointly with her husband for the same robbery. Can she be called by the prosecution against him?
options: No – a person jointly charged is not competent/compellable for the prosecution while still a co-accused
explanations: Correct (unless no longer liable to be convicted in the proceedings ⚠).

questions.scenario: In which case is a spouse compellable for the prosecution?
options: Criminal damage to the spouse's car
explanations: Correct: sexual offence against a person under 16.

questions.scenario: A couple divorced last year. The ex-wife is a witness against her ex-husband in a theft case. Which is correct?
options: She is not compellable because they were married
She is treated like any other witness (competent and compellable)

questions.scenario: Can a defendant be called as a witness for the prosecution in his own trial?
options: No, the accused is not competent for the prosecution

questions.scenario: PC LEE wants to refresh her memory in court from her pocket notebook. Under s. 139 CJA 2003, which is required?
options: The document records her recollection at the time and it was likely to be significantly better then
The notes were written by another officer

questions.scenario: Which witness is automatically eligible for special measures as an intimidated witness (unless they opt out)?
options: A complainant in a sexual offence case

questions.scenario: A 17-year-old witness of a robbery is eligible for special measures because…
options: they are under 18 and therefore a vulnerable witness

questions.scenario: Which of the following is NOT a special measure?
options: Allowing the witness not to be cross-examined at all

questions.scenario: What is hearsay under s. 114 CJA 2003?
options: Any evidence a witness gives in court
A statement not made in oral evidence in the proceedings, relied on as evidence of the matter stated

questions.scenario: A key witness died before the trial. Her statement may be admissible under…
explanations: s. 9 requires no objection; s. 116 covers unavailability.

questions.scenario: A witness refuses to give evidence through fear. Her statement may be admitted under s. 116…
options: only with the leave of the court

questions.scenario: Which of these is NOT a reason under s. 116 for a witness being unavailable?
options: Prefers not to come because of work
Outside the UK and not reasonably practicable to secure attendance
Cannot be found despite reasonable steps

questions.scenario: Under s. 114(1) CJA 2003, hearsay can be admitted if…
options: all parties agree to it being admissible

questions.scenario: Through how many gateways can a defendant's bad character be admitted under s. 101(1) CJA 2003?
The defendant tells the jury he has 'never been in trouble'. He has several convictions. Which gateway may allow them in?
The defendant attacks a prosecution witness's character, calling him a liar and a thief. Which gateway may be relevant?
explanations: He hasn't introduced his own character.

questions.scenario: For which gateways must the court exclude bad character evidence if admitting it would have such an adverse effect on fairness that it ought not to be admitted?
Evidence showing the defendant has a propensity to commit offences of the kind charged would usually go through…
Are spouses compellable for the DEFENCE of their spouse?
Is age, by itself, a bar to a child giving evidence?
options: No – the test is understanding questions and giving intelligible answers

questions.scenario: Pre-recorded cross-examination for vulnerable witnesses is provided by which section of YJCEA 1999?
A shop's routine computer records of sales are offered as evidence. Which hearsay provision is most relevant?
A spouse is compellable for the prosecution where the offence involves a threat of injury to…
options: the spouse or a person under 16

questions.scenario: Which statement about the defendant giving evidence is correct?
options: He gives evidence only on paper
He may give evidence in his own defence but cannot be compelled

questions.scenario: Res gestae is an example of…
options: a preserved common law hearsay exception

questions.scenario: Special measures for an intimidated witness may be available where the quality of evidence is likely to be diminished by…
options: fear or distress in connection with testifying
